category_title: 8-year-old student with ADHD (Combined Type) exhibiting disruptive classroom behaviors and social-emotional challenges
minimal_context: Alex and the tutor are sitting one-on-one at home to complete his daily homework assignments.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to sit down and complete your homework assignments for today.

STUDENT: I don't have any homework today. I lost my assignments anyway.

TUTOR: I have your worksheet right here. Please look at it and start working.

STUDENT: (Stands beside the desk and quickly scribbles down a few answers) There, I'm done. I skipped the rest.

TUTOR: You have a lot of missing answers and mistakes. You need to sit back down and finish the whole page.

STUDENT: (Becomes tearful) I can't do it! I'm just a bad kid! I'm very bad and my mom is going to send me to another country!

options.A: Decrease homework requirements to emphasize accuracy over quantity during independent work sessions.
options.B: Explore the relationship between 'fight' responses and anxiety, framing them into positive coping.
options.C: Extend homework sessions to one and a half hours, unlike typical 40-minute school lessons.
options.D: Develop critical consciousness through multicultural curricula addressing authentic issues of race, ethnicity, and class.
